The Authentic Name of Pachacámac

Scholarly reference for Pachacámac

Scholarly Transliteration

Pachacámac

No indigenous writing system is securely attested for individual incan names. The form shown is a modern scholarly transliteration.

ASCII Constraint

PACHACAMAC

Stripped of its identity, the name was reduced to plain Latin letters. The original orthography — stress, length, breathing — was erased by systems that only understand A-Z.

Unicode Restoration

Pachacámac

The Unicode restoration recovers what ASCII destroyed. This is philological accuracy — not decoration. The domain encodes to Punycode, but the browser displays the truth.

Punycode Encoding
pachacámac.com → xn--pachacmac-51a.com

The non-ASCII characters in Pachacámac are encoded while the ASCII remains visible. To the DNS, it is Punycode. To humanity, it is Pachacámac. PUNICODEX does not claim this domain is available; always verify status with a registrar.

Tier Classification

Why Pachacámac is classified as Tier-1

The Incan restoration Pachacámac preserves at least one distinctive feature its ASCII form loses — a diacritic or a distinctive letter that marks the original phonology. This makes it a single-tier Tier-1 name.

Stress
Preserved
Acute or circumflex accent marks the pitch stress of the original.

—
